end.summary:
Plotted and read position-time graphs; identified slope as velocity.
Interpreted horizontal position-time lines as an object standing still.
Calculated velocity from an x-t slope: 30/10 = 3 m/s.
Calculated acceleration from a v-t slope: 12/4 = 3 m/s².
Calculated displacement from a v-t triangle area: 24 m.
end.parentNote: Ira practised reading position-time and velocity-time graphs as motion stories. They used slope for velocity and acceleration, and area under a velocity-time graph for displacement; the calculations were correct. They also explained that a horizontal position-time line means the object is waiting or standing still. At home, ask them to describe one graph in words before calculating from it.
